body.statement: For a successful single-hazard design, the deterministic \(\mathsf A_1\) reconstruction is rational and continuously differentiable with finite derivative at every positive population law, equals \(Q\) there, and its empirical observed-cell plug-in estimator is consistent and asymptotically Gaussian with covariance \(DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\). The known-\(e\) audit-table form follows by composition with its fixed linear map.
body.justification: Positive denominators make the returned map rational and smooth at every legal population point, yielding standard finite-table inference centered at the proved causal target.
body.gap: Full-follow-up double-sampling influence-function results do not cover this partial-bundle reconstruction.
body.consumer: A sufficient audited design obtains joint standard errors for the treatment-specific endpoint distribution without full trajectory recovery.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(\mathsf C_1=1\), the set \(\mathcal H(B)\) is nonempty by \(\text{def:criterion}\), and its lexicographically first pair \((d,\ell)\) depends only on the fixed design.  Equations (1)--(11) in \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\) express every coordinate of the returned reconstruction using finite sums, products, and ratios of pattern-table cells.  At a positive population law, all denominator functionals in (3)--(5) and (9) are strictly positive.  There is therefore an open neighborhood of the population table on which the same denominators remain nonzero.  On this neighborhood the reconstruction is rational and hence continuously differentiable with a finite derivative.

By \(\text{prop:audit-table-equivalence}\), known positive audit probabilities map the observed-cell vector to the pattern tables by a fixed finite linear transformation: audited cells are divided by the corresponding \(e_d(H_d)>0\), and the required routine marginals are finite sums.  Composing this linear map with the rational reconstruction gives the stated local map \(F\).  The recovery part of \(\text{thm:single-hazard-alternative}\) proves the population identity
\[
F(o)=Q;
\tag{24}
\]
it is not imposed by the definition of \(F\).

For consistency, enumerate the \(m\) structural observed cells.  By \(\text{ass:iid-sampling}\), each coordinate is an average of iid Bernoulli indicators, so
\[
\operatorname{Var}(\widehat o_{n,r})
=\frac{o_r(1-o_r)}n\le\frac1{4n}.
\]
For each \(r\), the pointwise inequality
\[
(\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r)^2
\ge\delta^2\mathbf 1\{|\widehat o_{n,r}-o_r|>\delta\}
\]
implies the corresponding probability bound after taking expectations.  Summing these bounds over the finite cells gives, for every \(\delta>0\),
\[
\Pr\{\|\widehat o_n-o\|_\infty>\delta\}
\le\sum_{r=1}^m
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(\widehat o_{n,r})}{\delta^2}
\le\frac{m}{4n\delta^2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{25}
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), continuity of \(F\) at \(o\) supplies a \(\delta>0\) such that \(\|v-o\|<\delta\) implies \(\|F(v)-F(o)\|<\eta\).  Equation (25), followed by (24), therefore proves \(F(\widehat o_n)\to Q\) in probability whenever the rational formula is defined.  Define the estimator arbitrarily when an empirical denominator vanishes.  Since every population denominator is positive, (25) shows that the probability of this modification tends to zero.

For the limit law, the cited finite-multinomial central limit theorem gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat o_n-o)\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top\right).
\tag{26}
\]
Finally, the cited multivariate delta method applied to (26) yields
\[
\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-F(o)\}\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).
\]
Substitution of the proved identity (24) gives the asserted centering at the causal target.  If one starts from inverse-probability audit tables, the initial table estimator is the same fixed linear image of \(\widehat o_n\); the chain rule composes \(DF(o)\) with that linear map, proving the final assertion.
